entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Meleager of Gadara was a poet and collector of epigrams who flourished in the 1st century BCE. He wrote some satirical prose, now lost, and some sensual poetry, of which 134 epigrams survive.

As a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of the Hellenistic period, Meleager was known for his eclectic tastes and his ability to bridge the gap between different artistic and cultural traditions.

Meleager's epigrams were widely admired and emulated during his lifetime, and he was often associated with the prominent poet Straton of Sardis. His works were also praised by the Roman poet Martial, who credited Meleager with influencing his own style.

Despite the enduring popularity of his epigrams, Meleager's life and works remain somewhat of an enigma, and much of his output has been lost to the ages. Nevertheless, his legacy as a master of the epigrammatic form continues to be celebrated by scholars and poetry enthusiasts alike.

"The art of saying a thing with a single word, and with a single word making a thing of the whole of life." - Meleager of Gadara

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Meleager of Gadara was a prominent poet and collector of epigrams who played a significant role in the development of Roman poetry and the transmission of Eastern cultural influences to the West during the Hellenistic period.
